def: Common Technical Document: the ICH M4 format that organises a marketing application into five modules.
Electronic CTD: the CTD delivered as PDF files in a fixed folder tree, described by an XML backbone that agencies read.
Non-eCTD electronic Submission: CTD-structured PDFs with bookmarks and tables of contents but no XML backbone or lifecycle.
The XML file (index.xml in v3.2.2) listing every document, where it sits in the CTD, and its lifecycle operation.
The Module 1 XML file for one region, e.g. us-regional.xml, carrying administrative metadata and Module 1 leaves.
One document entry in the backbone: a file reference plus its title, checksum, operation and attributes.
A heading in the CTD tree, written as an XML element. Leaves sit inside nodes.
An EU v3.2.2 mechanism to add an extra grouping level under a heading, e.g. to group files of one study.
The human-readable title shown to reviewers in the agency viewer. It is not the file name.
A fingerprint of a file's bytes (MD5 in v3.2.2, SHA-256 in v4.0) proving the file was not altered in transit.
What a leaf does to the lifecycle: new, replace, append or delete (v3.2.2).
The pointer from a replace, append or delete leaf to the earlier leaf it acts on, by sequence and leaf ID.
One submission package, numbered 0000, 0001, 0002 and so on. Each sequence is a separate folder.
What a reviewer sees today: the latest version of every document after all operations are applied.
Every leaf ever submitted, across all sequences, including replaced and deleted ones.
How much content goes in one file. ICH M4 granularity rules say which headings may be split into several documents.
STF: a US v3.2.2 XML file grouping the documents of one study in Modules 4 and 5 and tagging their roles.
eCTD v4.0: the placement of a document at a heading, which can be replaced or suspended independently of the document.
eCTD v4.0: the single XML message that replaces index.xml and regional XML.
An agency refusing a sequence before scientific review because it fails the validation criteria.
The US application form for an NDA, ANDA or BLA, placed in Module 1.1 with every submission to the application.
IR: a question from the US review team during review, answered by an amendment sequence.
A heading that appears once per drug substance/manufacturer (3.2.S), drug product (3.2.P) or indication (5.3.5), told apart by attributes.
The app's helper that flags documents too coarse (whole module in one file) or too fine (one test per file).
